text:
Parsing Variable Values
Starting off, we need to save the links for the API call.

l21<-"https://api.census.gov/data/2021/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json"
l22<-"https://api.census.gov/data/2022/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json"
l23<-"https://api.census.gov/data/2023/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json"
l24<-"https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json"

Next, we create a function that pulls our desired list of variables out of the API call, taking into account the ST/STATE difference between years.

getVars <- function(link){
  varReturn <- httr::GET(link)
  varParsed <- fromJSON(rawToChar(varReturn$content))
  varLlist <- varParsed$variables
  targetVars <- c("AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP", "JWMNP", "PWGTP", "FER", "HHL", "SCH", "SCHL", "SEX", "ST","STATE", "REGION", "DIVISION")
  availableVars <- intersect(targetVars, names(varLlist))
  varsFin <- varLlist[availableVars]
  
  return(varsFin[!sapply(varsFin, is.null)])
}

Now we run this function on our links, and save all of the lists into one big list.

varList21 <- getVars(l21)
varList22 <- getVars(l22)
varList23 <- getVars(l23)
varList24 <- getVars(l24)
varLists <- list("y2021"=varList21,"y2022"=varList22,"y2023"=varList23,"y2024"=varList24)

Finally, we save the data and remove extraneous R objects.

saveRDS(varLists, file="data/varLists.rds")
remove(l21,l22,l23,l24,getVars)

Graphical Summaries
The final code writing section: creating a generic plot function. This is a fairly easy call to ggplot.

plot_census <- function(df, cat_var, num_var) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x=.data[[cat_var]], y=.data[[num_var]], weight=PWGTP)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(
      x=cat_var,
      y=num_var,
      title=paste("Boxplot of", num_var, "by", cat_var)) +
    theme_minimal()
}
